title: Morocco Signs Deal For Autonomous 2,000km Strike Drone
source_used: iAfrica (the item's outlet, Aviation Business Middle East, returned HTTP 403)
key_facts: Morocco's National Defense Administration and French firm Harmattan AI signed a letter of intent to develop IRIFI, an autonomous deep-strike drone with a stated range of up to 2,000 km.
It was signed at the opening of the Marrakech Air Show.
No contract value, timeline or production commitment has been disclosed.
Commanders designate authorised targets and set mission parameters before launch; the system then carries out the mission autonomously within those limits.
Navigation does not depend on satellite positioning, with optical terminal guidance.
Harmattan AI says critical components will be developed and produced in Morocco; the report notes the split between the two countries has not been specified.
The letter builds on a strategic partnership signed in June 2026.
quote_evidence: Morocco’s National Defense Administration and French defence technology company Harmattan AI have signed a letter of intent to jointly develop IRIFI, an autonomous deep-strike system with a stated range of up to 2,000 kilometres.
The agreement was signed at the opening of the Marrakech Air Show.
No contract value, timeline or production commitment has been disclosed.
why_it_matters_hint: An intent to develop, not a purchase: the drone does not yet exist as a product.
event_date: Opening of the Marrakech Air Show (about 7 Oct 2026; the date is not stated in the text)
notes: Pool headline said 'signs deal'; the text shows a letter of intent only. The 2,000 km range is a stated figure.
